previousValue.headline: AI Video Ads Generator for Ad Tests
previousValue.description: Use the AI video ads generator to test one opening at a time. Upload one photo, keep the length the same, and download the versions you want to run.

mainEntity.name: What does the AI video ads generator do?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tool that makes a short video ad from a product, a prompt, or a link, with a script, a presenter, and a voice. You do not film, and you do not need an edit bay.

mainEntity.name: How do I create a video ad to test?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a photo or paste the product link, and name the opening you want. Download the shape this test uses.

mainEntity.name: What should I look for when I pick a tool for ad tests?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pick a tool that can make a second opening of the same product from the photo you already have, with no new shoot.

mainEntity.name: Do I pay to make each version?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A clip is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

mainEntity.name: Can I run the file as a paid ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The download has no watermark. It can run as a paid placement and sit on the product page.

mainEntity.name: Which frames can I download, and where can they run?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use 9:16 on a phone screen, 1:1 in a feed, and 16:9 when the screen is wide. 4:3 and 3:4 are for a placement that lists them. A second shape is a different test.

mainEntity.name: Can I test ads for more than one product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if each product has its own photo. Reuse one opening as the note. Many products still means one file each.

mainEntity.name: Should I stop filming with people I hire?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Keep a filmed spot when you want a person you hired on camera. Use a generated file when you are still choosing the first second.

mainEntity.name: Can a generated ad be turned down by the ad account?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, for the same reasons any ad can. If the line sounds like a customer wrote a review, say so the way that app currently asks. Read the rules before you raise the budget.

mainEntity.name: How many versions should a small shop run?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with a few, often three. More than that splits a small budget so far that no version gets a fair chance to play.

mainEntity.name: What should I test first?

acceptedAnswer.text: The opening. It decides whether anyone watches the rest. Keep the product, the length, and the shape the same until that result is clear.

mainEntity.name: Can I change the price on only one version?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. While you are testing the video or the photo, put the same words, the same price, and the same music on every file. Test the offer in a later round, on its own.

mainEntity.name: Where do the numbers come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From the ad account, after each version has played. The test does not invent a winner. You read who stayed, who clicked, and what a sale cost.

mainEntity.name: What if the ad account barely shows one version?

acceptedAnswer.text: That version was not tested. Wait until each file has had a real chance to play, or the comparison is noise.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to say the presenter is generated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when the ad could be read as a real customer's review. Follow that platform's disclosure rule.

previousValue.headline: Amazon Main Image Rules for Every Listing
previousValue.description: Meet Amazon's main-image rules with one pure-white setup for the whole catalog. Keep the product large, check the corners, then send the files.

mainEntity.name: What does Amazon want on the main image?

acceptedAnswer.text: The product you ship, large in the square, on white that reads 255 on red, green, and blue. A sticker, a badge, or an extra object stays off this picture. The product should fill most of the frame.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the main image breaks the rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: The listing can drop out of search until you replace that main image with a compliant square. A photo of the product in use belongs in a later spot, not in the main square.

mainEntity.name: How do I get a pure white background from a phone photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload your product photo, remove its background, set the square to pure white, and check every corner before posting the main image.

mainEntity.name: Can I do this for many products together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. After the first product is right, the next colors can use that same square. Each color keeps that product's own shape, color, and label.

mainEntity.name: Can my shop system start the white image?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. If your shop system already lists every item, it can send the photo and ask for the white square. You still compare each file with the product in your hand. The API is not a separate install.

mainEntity.name: Why does my white background look gray on Amazon?

acceptedAnswer.text: The corners are not full white. Check them with a color picker and ask for 255 on red, green, and blue again. A gray haze at the edge is enough for the square to fail.

mainEntity.name: Can an image made here be my Amazon main image?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if it shows the real product, on pure white, with nothing extra drawn on. Compare it with the item you ship before you upload it to Seller Central.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does one white image use?

acceptedAnswer.text: 24 credits. The cost shows before the job starts. If it does not finish, those credits come back. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

mainEntity.name: Will the product's shape change?

acceptedAnswer.text: It keeps the shape in the photo you uploaded. If a strap, a buckle, or the label shifts, try again from a sharper photo before you publish the file.

mainEntity.name: What if the product is white, clear, or a set?

acceptedAnswer.text: Light it from the side so the edge still reads, and keep every piece that ships in the frame. A pale product on white needs that edge or it can disappear.

mainEntity.name: What can image to video do with a product photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: It turns a still into a short video. For sellers, one product photo can become a clip with motion, a voiceover, and captions you can post.

mainEntity.name: How does a photo become a video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload the image and describe the motion you want. Add a script and a voiceover, plus on-screen text, and review the clip before you post it.

mainEntity.name: What do you gain by making video from a photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: More ads from the photos you already own. You skip the shoot, and you can make another version whenever the current one goes stale. A 6-second clip is 24 credits.

mainEntity.name: Can I post these clips on social?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Size each clip for TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts, and post it as an ad or as a regular unpaid post.

mainEntity.name: How can a store use this for product marketing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Show the product in action, reveal a before-and-after, run social video ads, or add a video to a marketplace listing. Each one starts from the same photo.

mainEntity.name: Can I make explainers and tutorials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Keep one AI actor and one script style for every lesson, so feature walkthroughs look consistent without re-recording.

mainEntity.name: Can I add a voiceover or an AI actor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Write your own script or let the tool draft one, pick a voice, and add an AI actor to present the product on camera.

mainEntity.name: Which aspect ratios can I pick?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose 9:16 for TikTok, Reels, and Stories, 1:1 for the feed, or 16:9 for YouTube. 4:3 and 3:4 are there too.

previousValue.description: Make a beauty UGC ad from one product photo. Show a routine or a shade, skip the creator wait, and download a clip for the feed or a paid beauty ad.

previousValue.name: How to Make a Beauty Ad in 3 Simple Steps

step.name: Upload a Beauty Product
step.text: Drop in a link, a photo, or the product details. The ad can start from that alone.

step.name: Choose an AI Actor
step.text: Choose an AI actor whose look fits your buyers, with a range of skin tones and styles for your beauty ad.

step.name: Add a Spoken Voice and Captions
step.text: Generate your complete beauty ad with a spoken line, captions, and the product in use, ready for the channels you sell on.

mainEntity.name: Can one product photo become a beauty ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload a straight-on photo or paste a product link, then ask for a routine, a shade swipe, an unboxing, or a review-style clip.

mainEntity.name: Can I show a before-and-after of skin?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A generated face is not proof of what a product does to skin. Show how it is applied, the texture, and the package. Leave skin results out of the ad.

mainEntity.name: Will the clip match my foundation or lipstick shade?

acceptedAnswer.text: Color follows your photo and the words you use. Shoot in daylight and name the shade in plain words, such as warm beige. If the color is off, make another version.

mainEntity.name: Can I put a price or a promo code on the image?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You type the price, the code, and the shade name. The spoken line and captions come with the clip, and you can fix them in the editor before download.

mainEntity.name: What photo should I upload for skincare?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a straight-on shot, label toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands in the frame. Glossy tubes and glass pick up glare, so use window light instead of a flash.

mainEntity.name: How long should a beauty ad be, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A 6-second clip spends 24 credits, 10 seconds spends 40, 15 seconds spends 60, and 30 seconds spends 120. A still image is 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. The screen shows that cost before you start. If the job fails, those credits come back.

mainEntity.name: Can I run the clips as paid beauty ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in paid ads. Keep ingredient text accurate, and do not invent a skin result. Add offer text where you can check it.

mainEntity.name: How is this different from hiring a creator?

acceptedAnswer.text: You spend credits on your plan, not a creator fee or extra edit rounds. Upload one photo or paste a link, pick an AI avatar, and post the clip as an ad.

mainEntity.name: Does the beauty clip include a voice and captions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The job can include a spoken line and captions, and you can fix both in the editor before you download.

mainEntity.name: What should an Amazon main image show?

mainEntity.name: What happens if an Amazon photo breaks the image rules?

acceptedAnswer.text: A main photo that still shows the room can be held back, and the listing can leave search until you replace that file. A prop can sit on a later image, not on the main one.

mainEntity.name: How do I get a white Amazon main image from a photo I already have?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload the photo you already have and put the product on white. The old background comes off, the edges stay with the product, and you download a finished file. A photo is 24 credits, shown before you start.

mainEntity.name: Can I prepare many Amazon photos in one run?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Send the whole line through one batch, lifestyle frames included. Each file spends credits, the cost shows first, and a failed job returns those credits. You can also run that batch through the API.

mainEntity.name: Can my catalog tool request the Amazon images?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. When a new product is saved, your catalog tool can request the image through the API. You choose when it goes into Seller Central. We never sign in to the seller account.

mainEntity.name: What other Amazon images should I add?

acceptedAnswer.text: A close-up, a sense of size, and the item in use. A hand in the frame helps the shopper see the scale. Those frames come after the white main image.

mainEntity.name: Can I put my own words on the pictures after I download them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Add the words yourself after download, and only on images after the main one. The main image stays free of badges and slogans.

mainEntity.name: Can I make a video for the Amazon listing without booking a shoot?

mainEntity.name: Will you upload the finished photos into Amazon for me?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Download the files and add them in Seller Central yourself. We do not connect to your seller login.

mainEntity.name: What does a video ads generator produce?

acceptedAnswer.text: A spoken ad from a product photo or a product page, with a script, an AI actor, and a voice. You pick from 53 AI actors. You do not film a set.

mainEntity.name: How does a shop build the video ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with a product photo or its page. Approve the drafted sentence, change a word if the product differs, then download. You can edit captions, swap the voice, or add a track from the music library.

mainEntity.name: Which kind of tool should a shop use for paid ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use one built for ads you can run: a script, an AI actor, a voice, and the sizes TikTok and Meta expect. This one does that from a photo or a product link, including a batch of products.

mainEntity.name: Do I pay before I can make the first ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You pick a paid plan, then make the first ad. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

mainEntity.name: Are commercial rights included on a paid plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. On a paid plan the clip can be the ad you fund. The file has no watermark, and you do not need a separate creator license.

mainEntity.name: Which frame sizes and placements can the file use?

acceptedAnswer.text: A phone ad wants 9:16, and a square feed wants 1:1. 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4 are there when the placement asks. You can download the file or send it toward TikTok, Meta, or Google Ads.

mainEntity.name: Can every product in the catalog get its own ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each product can get an ad from its own photo or page. Shop software you already use can send that list. Every clip still spends credits, and a failed job returns them.

mainEntity.name: How do these compare with ads filmed by creators?

acceptedAnswer.text: Book a creator when you need a person filmed with the product itself. Use the generated ad when you are still choosing which opening to buy. Test more than one opening.

mainEntity.name: Will Meta or TikTok reject a generated clip?

acceptedAnswer.text: Read that ad account's current rule before you fund the clip. If a viewer could think a buyer filmed their own order, add the label that account asks for. Keep the scene true to the product you uploaded.
